title: Tumor-associated astrocytes augment cholesterol synthesis to support glioblastoma growth through alternatively spliced QKI isoforms.
authors: Wu, Runxin; Yu, Xiaozhou; Song, Xiao; He, Qiu; Walker, Maya; Sisbarro, Derek; Horbinski, Craig; Tiek, Deanna; Hu, Bo; Zhang, Nu; Cheng, Shi-Yuan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究GBM相关星形胶质细胞中QKI异构体转换通过QKI-5-SREBP2轴促进胆固醇合成支持肿瘤生长，虽涉及AlphaFold3结构预测蛋白互作，但核心是RNA结合蛋白与转录因子SREBP2的蛋白-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI/物理模拟方法用于结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with limited treatment options. Tumor-associated astrocytes (TAAs) are crucial components of the GBM microenvironment, yet the contribution of alternative splicing (AS) in TAAs to tumor progression remains unclear. METHODS: Transcriptomic and molecular analyses of GBM-associated astrocytes revealed a GBM-induced isoform switch in the RNA-binding protein Quaking (QKI) from the QKI-6 isoform to QKI-5 isoform. The biological role of QKI-5 was examined through gain- and loss-of-function approaches in human astrocytes and coculture systems with patient-derived glioma stem-like cells (GSCs). In vitro proliferation and sphere-formation assays, along with in vivo orthotopic xenograft models, were used to evaluate tumor growth. Immunoprecipitation and AlphaFold3 structural prediction were performed to investigate the mechanistic interaction between QKI-5 and sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2). RESULTS: GBM-induced QKI-5 interacts with SREBP2 to transcriptionally activate cholesterol metabolic enzymes, enhancing astrocyte-derived cholesterol production and promoting GBM growth. Knockdown of QKI-5 or inhibitors for SREBP2-driven signaling suppressed astrocyte-mediated tumor-supportive effects in vitro and in vivo. CONCLUSION: QKI-5 drives astrocytic metabolic reprogramming via the QKI-5-SREBP2 axis, fostering a cholesterol-rich tumor microenvironment that supports GBM progression. Targeting this pathway offers a potential therapeutic strategy.
abstract_zh: 背景：胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）是一种高度侵袭性脑肿瘤，治疗选择有限。肿瘤相关星形胶质细胞（TAAs）是GBM微环境的关键组成部分，但TAAs中可变剪接（AS）对肿瘤进展的贡献尚不清楚。方法：对GBM相关星形胶质细胞的转录组和分子分析揭示了一种GBM诱导的RNA结合蛋白Quaking（QKI）亚型转换，从QKI-6亚型转换为QKI-5亚型。通过在人星形胶质细胞及与患者来源的胶质瘤干细胞样细胞（GSCs）共培养系统中的功能获得和功能丧失方法，检测了QKI-5的生物学作用。采用体外增殖和球体形成实验，以及体内原位异种移植模型，评估肿瘤生长。通过免疫沉淀和AlphaFold3结构预测，研究QKI-5与甾醇调节元件结合蛋白2（SREBP2）之间的机制性相互作用。结果：GBM诱导的QKI-5与SREBP2相互作用，转录性激活胆固醇代谢酶，增强星形胶质细胞来源的胆固醇产生，并促进GBM生长。敲低QKI-5或使用SREBP2驱动信号传导的抑制剂，在体外和体内均抑制了星形胶质细胞介导的肿瘤支持效应。结论：QKI-5通过QKI-5-SREBP2轴驱动星形胶质细胞代谢重编程，营造富含胆固醇的肿瘤微环境，支持GBM进展。靶向该通路提供了一种潜在的治疗策略。
